text: Deficit irrigation of field tomatoes: yield and water use over two seasons
Ingrid Halvorsen, Chidi Okafor
Northfield Agricultural Institute, Norway; Coastal Plains Research Station, Nigeria
Abstract

Deficit irrigation supplied 70% of crop evapotranspiration to field tomatoes over the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Marketable yield fell by 6% against full irrigation, while water use fell by 28%, so that water productivity rose from 18.4 to 23.9 kg per cubic metre.
Introduction

Irrigation accounts for most of the fresh water withdrawn in the study region, and the allocations to farms were cut in 2023. Deficit irrigation, which supplies less water than the crop uses, has kept yields of other crops close to those of full irrigation [1].

Discussion
The loss of yield under deficit irrigation was small against the water saved, and the fruit of the deficit plots had a higher sugar content.
